reason: Reproduced exactly, on both grounds, and it is a genuinely new mechanism rather than a re-run. THE REPRO. master.html?v=paper&state=owner-flight at 1024x800: open the editor on Venue walk-through, the pane settles at .b-plan scrollTop 997 and .b-gapNote reads '19 September · 65 days away'. Press −1: scrollTop is still exactly 997, nothing has scrolled, and the note becomes 'Nothing is planned until 1 August.' It stays wrong through every further press; nudging the pane one pixel (scrollTop 998) restores '16 September · 62 days away'. Byte-identical on ?v=ink at 1024x800 (997 -> same revert -> same 1px recovery). At 1440x960 the same press at scrollTop 917 turns '5 September · 51 days away' into 'Nothing is planned until 1 August.' and the 1px nudge restores it. So the finding's numbers are its own, and correct. THE MECHANISM IS AS DESCRIBED, and it is broader than the finding claims. render-b.js:356-365 writes note.textContent = gapSentence(items[0].getAttribute('data-date')) unconditionally, and that write sits in place(), which is called by setAway() (render-b.js:734) after every stepper press AND by the variant's settle() (render-b.js:2042-2044, 'for (i...) place(all[i])'), which render-core.js:168 runs on the debounced resize, on fonts.ready and on every C.settle(). The scroll-aware writer speak() (render-b.js:1334-1361) is bound only to window and .b-plan scroll (1366-1368). I confirmed two further triggers the finding did not test: with the pane held at scrollTop 900 at 1440, a bare viewport resize 1440->1439 reverts the line with scrollTop unchanged at 900; and typing into #b-edit-title with the pane at 413 reverts it on the first keystroke. Because nothing scrolls, no scroll event follows and the false sentence persists indefinitely. NOT SETTLED. The nearest ledger item, ux--the-pinned-line-and-the-lead-tick-name-nothing (round 9), was killed on 15/15 samples showing the line always names the topmost row in the pane - but every one of those samples was taken by scrolling, never by editing while scrolled, which is the only path that produces this. That is new evidence meeting the stated objection. taste--pinned-label-stops-naming-what-is-under-it (round 8) was about the label/date arithmetic, and ui--received-desk-readout-goes-stale (round 9) was about state=desk never calling wireOwner. Different mechanisms. NOT A GATE RESTATEMENT. All four .b-gapNote assertions in interaction-check.mjs (L245 phone boundary, L376 post-stepper at scrollTop 0, L1940-1961 scroll-out-and-back, L2699-2704 the round-7 anti-snapshot check) either never scroll the pane or never edit while it is scrolled, so none of them can see this. The gate's own label - 'and goes back to the gap when the gap is on screen' - states the rule this violates: after the press the gap is roughly a thousand pixels above the fold. THE FIX WORKS AND IS SAFE. I ran the proposed patch by intercepting render-b.js at request time (nothing in the lab was edited): exposing speak as root.__gapSpeak and calling it at the end of place(). Patched, the 1024x800 repro on paper and on ink reads '18 September · 64 days away' then '17 September · 63 days away' across two presses instead of reverting; the 1440x960 case correctly holds '5 September · 51 days away' because the row it names did not move. Re-ran all four gapNote gate assertions patched and unpatched: identical results in every one (L376 gap 'Nothing is planned until 1 August.' at scrollTop 0; L1940 atRest/scrolled/back all match; L2693 moved === back === 'Nothing is planned until 25 July.'; L245 phone unchanged). The empty-plan guard survives - deleting every spare moment leaves 'Nothing is planned until 3 October.' - because speak() returns early on !rows.length, and the phone and 768 bands are untouched because speak() returns early when .b-stick is not sticky. Real, specific, cheap, and it removes a plain falsehood one line under the 79-day figure it is meant to qualify, on the owner's most frequent action.
sharpenedFix: Two lines, no structural change. (1) In wireOwner, immediately before 'var onScroll = function () {' (render-b.js:1363), add: root.__gapSpeak = speak;  (2) In place(), immediately after the existing note.textContent write block closes (render-b.js:365), add: if (field && field.__gapSpeak) field.__gapSpeak();  Reuse the 'field' variable already declared at render-b.js:356 - do not re-derive it with measureEl.closest as the finding's draft does. Two corrections to the finding's text for the build note: the repainting writer is place(), not relay() (there is no relay() in the file); and its reach is wider than the stepper - the same revert fires on the debounced resize, on fonts.ready and on every keystroke in the title field, because settle() calls place() for every .b-measure (render-b.js:2042). Order matters: leave place()'s own write in and call speak() after it, so the items.length === 0 branch ('Nothing is planned yet.') still lands - speak() returns early on an empty measure and would otherwise leave the node stale. No guard on width is needed: speak() already returns early when .b-stick is not position:sticky, so phone and the 701-1023 band are untouched, and field.__gapSpeak is undefined on every non-owner measure.
